pageCache.pageTitle: Great Hollands Primary School - Personal Development
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
At Great Hollands Primary School we recognise that the personal development of pupils is a fundamental part of our academic and pastoral work. It is our intention to create good local, national and global citizens, who develop good character and resilience. To this end, we aim to develop pupils spiritually, morally, socially and culturally and ensure that they are treated as individuals whilst doing this. We aim to teach pupils about British values, mutual respect and tolerance.
We aim to deliver spiritual, moral, social and cultural education through all aspects of school life; curriculum, extra-curricular activities, the pastoral system, assemblies as well as themed events.
Our Personal Development provision incorporates both PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) and SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural). We follow the recommendations laid out by the Department for Education and the PSHE Association.

pageCache.pageTitle: Great Hollands Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Thinking and Learning Together; Achieving Forever
Thank you for your interest in Great Hollands Primary School.
We are a vibrant school full of enthusiastic learners. Our children are at the heart of every decision we make; they motivate and inspire us each day to achieve endless possibilities. The opportunities the school provides for them are relevant to their needs, both now and for the future. As part of Maiden Erlegh Trust, we reflect the trust values to aim high, be inclusive and work together in all we do.
In recent years, Great Hollands Primary School has transformed itself, achieving so much success in a short space of time. We have developed a culture and ethos within the school that is of high aspirations, care and a relentless drive to be better and to provide our children with the best start in life.
We aim to instil a passion for life-long learning in all our children. Most important to us, however, is the happiness of each child, and alongside our academic excellence, we teach emotional resilience strategies to help support our children to develop the character and confidence needed to navigate our ever-changing world.
We provide our pupils with the skills and knowledge to thrive in this modern world. We are rightly proud of our achievements in Reading, Writing and Maths, yet we offer so much more. Our curriculum is based on a mastery approach and every lesson and experience is tailored towards ensuring that all our pupils reach their full potential. We nurture the whole child, striving to develop resilience, confidence and character in our children whilst developing a drive to succeed and keep themselves safe, healthy and happy so they can play a positive and active role in the world.
In so many ways, the education at Great Hollands ensures a solid and successful foundation for our children to access their next phase of education from 11 years of age. Strong partnerships with parents are part of our success, as is our committed, dedicated and talented school teaching team who strive diligently to continually improve the school for our children.
Our fabulous school environment provides stunning learning spaces throughout the school, redesigned and developed for 21st Century learning. Across the school, our spaces are equipped with a host of modern systems, including moveable walls and interactive touchscreen displays. These bright, airy spaces alongside our amazing teaching team give our children from Nursery upwards a superb start to their learning journey with us.
I couldn’t be prouder to lead a team who are committed to ensuring each child’s individuality shines through and for them to reach their full potential. We are creating something very special in our school and I would strongly encourage you to visit us, to experience for yourself the magic of Great Hollands Primary School.
Richard Ferris, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Great Hollands Primary School - Nursery Admissions
pageCache.text:
Nursery Admissions
Children are offered a place at our Nursery starting the term after their third birthday, subject to availability.
You can complete our application form to go on the waiting list for a Nursery place at any time. The form can be found here: Nursery Application Form
The timetable below indicates the timescales for parents making an application to our Nursery for a place following their third birthday.
If the child is born on or between
Applications should be made no later than
Eligibility for a nursery place (term after the child’s third birthday)
1st April and 31st August
Autumn Term (September)
1st September and 31st December
Spring Term (January)
1st January and 31st March
Applications made after the closing date will also be considered, but places cannot be guaranteed.
‘In-term’ applications from families for new starters (for example, if moving to the area) will be assessed on an individual basis.
If you have any questions regarding Nursery admissions, please get in touch with the school office on 01344 424911 or by email to ghpsoffice@maidenerleghtrust.org.

pageCache.text:
Emergency Closure Information and Remote Learning Provision
Closing the school is not a decision that is taken lightly because of the inconvenience it causes parents and carers and the loss of time for children in school. However, there may be times when there is no alternative.
We will always endeavour to give as much notice as possible, but sometimes health and safety risks, or rapidly changing weather conditions may make this difficult. Our aim will always be to avoid unnecessary closure.
Procedures
If it is necessary to close, there are several places to get information.
The school website will be updated.
Closure
If the closure is snow-related, and it has snowed before the start of the school day, road conditions may stop enough staff getting in to school. The school will decide whether to;
If the school is open, but severe weather comes in during the day, the school may decide to close the school early. The deciding factors for this would be:
Fully close the school.
Children's safety,
Remote Learning
If the school has to close to pupils for more than 1 day, then work will be set and made accessible either by Google Classroom, email or on the website to support parents in keeping learning happening at home.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At Great Hollands, our broad, planned and relevant curriculum brings learning to life through investigations and open-ended learning, providing an emphasis on both knowledge and skills to help our children develop a thirst for learning.
Learning is carefully sequenced and linked across subjects, ensuring that over time our children both know and remember more. At Great Hollands, our curriculum: recognises children's prior learning; provides first-hand learning experiences; and is underpinned by the academic rigour needed to ensure depth of learning. Throughout the school, our curriculum is complimented by learning opportunities to ensure our children's spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
In Key Stage 1 we use the Read, Write Inc scheme to assist in the teaching of phonics. More information about the scheme can be found at www.ruthmiskin.com/en/find-out-more/parents/
Our FAQ for parents about how we teach reading using the programme can be found here.
After the children have completed the Read, Write Inc scheme, they move on to accessing a wealth of reading books through the Renaissance online library.
Our key aim is that when children leave us at the end of Year 6, they are secondary school ready and equipped with the following:
Parents have the right to choose to withdraw their child from Religious Education. Requests to do so should be made in writing to the school office, marked for the attention of the Headteacher.
If you require further information regarding the curriculum, please contact Ms York, via the School Office.
